small_guidance:
- The kernel has each program redo the full ConvTranspose2d compute then sum-reduces; HW=256*256=65536 per (N,OC tile) is large. Try larger BLOCK_HW (256, 512) with IC_TILE=64 and num_warps=8/num_stages=3 to better amortize the weight loads which are reused across all HW tiles.
- Hoist the weight loads outside the HW loop: for a fixed (pid_oc, kh, kw, ic_tile) the weight tile is invariant across hw_start iterations, so restructure loop nesting to (kh, kw, ic) outermost and HW innermost, loading w once per (kh,kw,ic) and accumulating partial sums into `sum_acc` directly via tl.sum, skipping the `acc` materialization.
- Drop bias from the inner accumulator; add `bias * HW * inv_area * multiplier` once at the end (bias contribution to the mean is just bias * multiplier).
large_guidance:
- Split into two kernels: (1) a proper im2col-style ConvTranspose2d GEMM that writes the full (N, OC, OH, OW) tensor in channels-last layout with one program per (N, OC tile, HW tile), and (2) a fast spatial-reduction kernel that produces (N, OC) means with multiplier folded in. This separates the heavy GEMM (which wants tl.dot on big tiles) from the reduction (which wants wide BLOCK_HW and small register footprint), and lets each be tuned independently.
- Alternatively, formulate as scatter-add: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile) computes input*weight outer product and scatter-adds into the output grid; combined with a separate mean kernel this matches the natural ConvTranspose2d dataflow and avoids the gather-side stride-divisibility masking that wastes lanes (only 1/(SH*SW)=1/4 of (kh,kw,oh,ow) combinations are valid in the current gather form).
- If keeping the fused single-kernel design, make it persistent over HW with the GEMM-K (IC*KH*KW) axis as the inner loop and accumulate the scalar sum directly, never materializing the (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_HW) tile — use tl.dot with K=IC_TILE and reduce its result along HW immediately, so register pressure stays bounded and BLOCK_HW can grow to 256+.
